text: The moon rose slow above the gum trees tall.
Sunny sat still in the cool and quiet dark.
High on a branch, something did not move at all —
a shape like an old grey broken bit of bark.
It was a tawny frogmouth, still as stone,
with feathers like the wood on which he sat.
Two golden eyes blinked slowly, wide and calm.
“Good evening,” he whispered. “Come and sit a while.”
Sunny climbed up on a soft and mossy stone
and looked up at the wise and quiet bird.
“How are you so still?” the little quokka asked.
“I listen,” said the frogmouth, “to the night.”
He heard the crickets sing their gentle song,
the leaves that whispered, and the soft warm breeze.
So Sunny listened too, and closed her eyes,
and heard the quiet breathing of the bush.
The stars came out like tiny silver lamps,
scattered soft across the deep and velvet sky.
The frogmouth ruffled up his cosy wings.
“The night will watch you sleep,” he softly said.
Sunny yawned a great big sleepy yawn
and found a bed of leaves beneath the tree.
The bush was calm. The moon was gentle-bright.
Everything was still, and safe, and slow.
Her eyes grew heavy, blinking like the bird's —
one slow blink… then another… then no more.
And Sunny slept beneath the frogmouth's watch,
as safe as any creature of the night.
Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, quiet frogmouth.
Goodnight, sleepy bush. Goodnight, little one.
